### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2ca75a38a3d40cec9eca69c63834cb6f4d1d512f` — the merge of head `175ff5aaf46fe006159955945e5697a7039c1442` into base `45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2ca75a38a3d40cec9eca69c63834cb6f4d1d512f && git checkout 2ca75a38a3d40cec9eca69c63834cb6f4d1d512f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344 175ff5aaf46fe006159955945e5697a7039c1442 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344 && git merge --no-ff 175ff5aaf46fe006159955945e5697a7039c1442

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45dee177b7454b58ccce8d440fc0a8862f774344` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `175ff5aaf46fe006159955945e5697a7039c1442`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T13:33Z
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5 (area S3 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

Read at the head: the 8 files (net diff against main: +389/−27), the commit list, and the recycle-bin code the new text cites (`objectql/src/recycle-bin/capture.ts`, `retention.ts`, `rest/src/recycle-bin-routes.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts`).

1. **Premise measured, and the text now matches it.** Every fact in `DELETE_RECYCLE_BIN_FACT` was checked against the cited code. A by-id delete of a business object is captured, and the platform namespaces `sys_`, `cloud_` and `ai_` are not (`hasPlatformObjectPrefix`, `capture.ts`). Retention is `OS_RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS` or the host's resolver, else `RECYCLE_BIN_DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` = 30 (`retention.ts`). The restore route `POST /api/v1/data/:object/recycle-bin/:entryId/restore` is on the REST ledger. "No MCP tool restores" is true of the tool registry. The old "permanent" wording is gone from both tool descriptions, both confirmation refusals, the served skill text, and §5 of `wire-format.mdx`.
2. **The answer change is additive and right.** The stdio bridge now passes `onRecycleBinEntry`, the protocol's `deleteData` member, so both transports answer `recycleBinEntryId` the same way. `delete_records` adds `recycleBinEntries` (and the same key on a fault's `progress`), present only when non-empty. Nothing about what is deleted, or about the confirmation gate, moves. `Clause-②: no` is right: no accepted input changes, and the reply gains an optional member. `paths` reads the face as declaration-only (`TIER_DEFAULT`), so no contract record is owed.
3. **The area's points.** (1) The `skill-md.ts` history (4dedcacb, its revert 72c39503, the re-apply 58d7c781) has a net effect equal to the fold; no force push, accepted. (2) The Console mirror: only the two delete bullets move, they are byte-identical to the served text (the mirror pin forces the change), and `@object-ui/console: patch` is in the changeset. Accepted as a mirror edit, not a ui feature. (3) The `wire-format.mdx` sentences are checked against the route and capture code: true. (4) The checks not measured locally are covered by CI on this head.
4. **Ablations.** Three ablations: the stdio member removed, `deleteEach` not collecting, and an invented entry id on the negative legs (a platform object, and a composition with no bin). Each names the mutation and the red output, and each restore is blob == HEAD. The negative legs pin "absent means permanent" both ways. Accepted.
5. The body says the cloud host's composition (bin registered, retention resolver) is NOT MEASURED, and the text hedges for exactly that case ("any record on a deployment with no recycle bin"). That is a fair hand-off for the cloud#3826 D3 decision, not a gap in this PR.

Gates not judged: at review time 1 check-run was in progress, 47 success, 11 skipped, none red. Landing needs every check green on this head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
